summary: float converts supported numeric text to a binary floating-point number.
documentation: float converts supported numeric text to a binary floating-point number. Surrounding whitespace and scientific notation are accepted. Invalid numeric text raises ValueError, while special strings can produce infinity or NaN.
inputs: An array of strings representing finite numeric values of magnitude below one million.
returns: A list of converted finite numbers.
caution: Binary floating point is approximate and is unsuitable for exact decimal currency arithmetic without a deliberate representation policy. This problem excludes invalid and nonfinite text.
scenarios: Import approximate sensor measurements from CSV text.
Convert duration fields in a local report preview.
Read scientific-notation measurements from an instrument export.
title: Parse finite measurements
problem: Convert each input string to a float and return the list. Inputs are valid finite numeric text, including surrounding spaces and exponent notation; no currency symbols or separators are supplied.
hint: Use float on every string; do not strip exponent notation.
goal: Use float() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
